title: A changing political horizon
paragraphs: Joseon’s return to routine was never a return to precisely the world that existed before the invasions. Military organization, fiscal pressures, debates over leadership, and international relations all acquired new urgency. The rise of powers beyond the northern border would soon test the kingdom again.

That is why reconstruction belongs at the beginning of late Joseon history. It establishes the circumstances in which later rulers and factions acted. From the villages recovering food production to the palace debating diplomacy, postwar life linked practical necessity to political choice.
